Providers, Credentials, and Offline Paths

Source: vignettes/providers.qmd

This article is the v0.5.0 status page for live services and no-network paths in catchmentACS. It answers three practical questions:

  1. Which services are implemented now?
  2. Which credentials are required?
  3. How can examples, tests, and reports run offline without accidentally calling Census or a routing provider?
library(catchmentACS)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)

old_options <- options(
  catchmentACS.progress = "off",
  catchmentACS.rate_first_default = FALSE
)
old_cache <- getOption("catchmentACS.cache_enabled", NULL)
on.exit(options(old_options), add = TRUE)
on.exit(options(catchmentACS.cache_enabled = old_cache), add = TRUE)
cacs_set_cache(FALSE, scope = "session")

About the data in this article

Every table and check here is built entirely from the package’s bundled inst/extdata fixtures (the synthetic legacy_2025_* objects and sample_alabama_subset), so this article renders with no Census, OSRM, ORS, or other network calls. These fixtures preserve the production calling contract (sites, drive-time polygons, tract-level ACS variables) but are synthetic and illustrative — included only for examples, tests, and reproducible package checks. They are not live Alabama policy estimates and must not be cited as real ACS results. The live code blocks below are shown for reference and marked non-evaluated; the one provider probe that does run points at an unreachable localhost port so it stays offline and deterministic. Any real analysis requires a fresh live run.

The short version: use provider = "osrm" for the easiest live route, use provider = "ors" when you have an ORS key, and use precomputed_isochrones plus acs whenever you need a completely offline run.

Which provider should I use?

OSRM and ORS are the two live routing paths in v0.5.0; Mapbox and r5r are reserved names that abort (see “Fail-loud reserved providers”). The decision is mostly about volume and whether you can stand up a local server:

You want to… Use Setup / key
Try the package or run a handful of sites provider = "osrm", osrm_mode = "demo" No key, no setup; shared public demo, can be slow or HTTP 429 rate-limited
Run a production batch (many sites, high res) provider = "osrm", osrm_mode = "docker" A local/self-hosted OSRM server (default http://0.0.0.0:5000/); no per-request quota
Avoid hosting OSRM but still route remotely provider = "ors" Optional openrouteservice package and a non-empty ors_api_key / ORS_API_KEY
Render docs, tests, or reproducible reports none — supply precomputed_isochrones = and acs = Fully offline; no key, no network (this article’s path)

Rules of thumb: the OSRM public demo is for convenience and low volume, not large jobs; a local OSRM docker endpoint is the production default once batches grow; ORS is the remote alternative when you have a key but cannot self-host. Mapbox and r5r are roadmap names only. The rest of this article covers credentials and each path in detail.

Credentials

Census API

ACS downloads are handled by tidycensus. Register a Census key once in an interactive R session:

tidycensus::census_api_key("YOUR_KEY_HERE", install = TRUE)

After restart, cacs_run() can call cacs_acs_prefetch() automatically in the full live path. A key is checked only after local validation and an ACS cache miss, before live tidycensus::load_variables() or tidycensus::get_acs() calls. If you pass acs = <sf> or hit a warm ACS cache entry, the live ACS stage is skipped and no Census key is required. v0.5.0 supports ACS5 end years 2009-2024 (2024 is the most recent vintage). See ?cacs_acs_prefetch for the prefetch contract and ?cacs_acs_validate for checking your own ACS table.

OSRM

OSRM is the default routing provider and needs no API key when using the public demo endpoint:

iso <- cacs_isochrone(
  sites = cacs_alabama_sites[1:3, ],
  drive_times = c(5, 10, 15),
  provider = "osrm",
  osrm_mode = "demo",
  res = 30L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

For heavier batch work, prefer a local or self-hosted OSRM endpoint. The public demo endpoint is shared infrastructure and can return HTTP 429 under load.

iso <- cacs_isochrone(
  sites = cacs_alabama_sites[1:3, ],
  drive_times = c(5, 10, 15),
  provider = "osrm",
  osrm_mode = "docker",
  `osrm.server` = "http://0.0.0.0:5000/",
  verbose = TRUE
)

When res is omitted on the public demo path, v0.5.0 protects the demo budget by resolving to a lower default than the self-hosted path. Pass res explicitly when reproducibility of polygon detail matters.

Before a long OSRM run, you can probe the endpoint with cacs_validate_osrm_endpoint(). It is a probe, not a gate: it never throws, returning a one-row tibble whose quota_ok flag and http_status you inspect (a known-saturated demo also emits a classed catchmentACS_warning_provider_quota_exhausted warning). The rendered vignette uses a known-unreachable localhost port, so the chunk stays offline and deterministic; the connection simply fails and quota_ok comes back FALSE.

cacs_validate_osrm_endpoint(
  server = "http://localhost:9",
  timeout = 1
)
# A tibble: 1 × 4
  endpoint           quota_ok response_ms http_status
  <chr>              <lgl>          <dbl>       <int>
1 http://localhost:9 FALSE           44.3          NA

For a real live preflight, omit server or point it at your self-hosted endpoint:

cacs_validate_osrm_endpoint()
cacs_validate_osrm_endpoint(server = "http://localhost:5000", timeout = 2)

ORS

ORS is implemented, but it requires the optional openrouteservice package and a non-empty API key supplied through ors_api_key or ORS_API_KEY.

Sys.getenv("ORS_API_KEY")

iso <- cacs_isochrone(
  sites = cacs_alabama_sites[1:3, ],
  drive_times = c(5, 10, 15),
  provider = "ors",
  ors_api_key = Sys.getenv("ORS_API_KEY"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Do not put API keys directly in scripts or vignettes. Use .Renviron, an environment manager, or CI secrets.

Offline bypass paths

cacs_run() selects its execution path from the presence or absence of two optional inputs:

tibble::tribble(
  ~execution_path, ~precomputed_isochrones, ~acs, ~network_behavior,
  "5-call", "not supplied", "not supplied",
  "Calls both routing provider and tidycensus.",
  "4-call-A", "supplied", "not supplied",
  "Skips routing provider; still calls tidycensus.",
  "4-call-B", "not supplied", "supplied",
  "Calls routing provider; skips tidycensus.",
  "3-call", "supplied", "supplied",
  "Skips both routing provider and tidycensus."
)
# A tibble: 4 × 4
  execution_path precomputed_isochrones acs          network_behavior
  <chr>          <chr>                  <chr>        <chr>
1 5-call         not supplied           not supplied Calls both routing provide…
2 4-call-A       supplied               not supplied Skips routing provider; st…
3 4-call-B       not supplied           supplied     Calls routing provider; sk…
4 3-call         supplied               supplied     Skips both routing provide…

The package vignettes use the 3-call path. The provider column still records the provenance of the precomputed isochrone, but no live provider is called while the article renders. The bundled legacy isochrones are synthetic buffered-circle polygons; provider = "osrm" records OSRM-style provenance metadata and does not imply a live OSRM request during rendering.

legacy_iso <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "legacy_2025_isochrones.rds", package = "catchmentACS"
))

legacy_iso |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(provider, provider_requested, profile,
        osm_snapshot_date, ring_topology)
# A tibble: 1 × 6
  provider provider_requested profile osm_snapshot_date ring_topology     n
  <chr>    <chr>              <chr>   <chr>             <chr>         <int>
1 osrm     osrm               car     2025-04-01        cumulative       60

Here is the smallest complete offline cacs_run() provider check:

legacy_sites <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "legacy_2025_sites.rds", package = "catchmentACS"
))
acs <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "sample_alabama_subset.rds", package = "catchmentACS"
))

site_id <- "AL_SITE_03"
iso_one <- legacy_iso |>
  filter(site_id == !!site_id, drive_time_min == 5L)
site_one <- legacy_sites |>
  filter(site_id == !!site_id)

out <- cacs_run(
  sites = site_one,
  state = "AL",
  year = 2023,
  drive_times = 5L,
  variables = unname(cacs_acs_default_vars),
  provider = "osrm",
  precomputed_isochrones = iso_one,
  acs = acs,
  weight_method = "area",
  output = "long",
  verbose = FALSE
)

attr(out, "cacs_run_provenance") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  select(execution_path, provider, bypass_iso, bypass_acs,
         weight_method, output_format)
  execution_path provider bypass_iso bypass_acs weight_method output_format
1         3-call     osrm       TRUE       TRUE          area          long

Use the same pattern in tests and reproducible reports: ship or load the exact sf ACS and isochrone inputs, pass them into cacs_run(), and record the resulting provenance attributes. For the same offline call worked into a full reporting table, see vignette("alabama-tutorial", package = "catchmentACS").

Fail-loud reserved providers

Mapbox and r5r are in the provider enum for compatibility and roadmap visibility, but they are intentionally not live routing paths in v0.5.0. Selecting either one raises a structured catchmentACS_error_credential condition rather than silently returning a placeholder. The check below catches that condition and reports only its class, so the chunk stays offline and prints no raw provider message.

demo_site <- tibble::tibble(
  site_id = "S01",
  lon = -86.80902,
  lat = 33.52203
)

condition_class <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch(
    {
      force(expr)
      "no_error"
    },
    catchmentACS_error = function(e) class(e)[[1L]],
    error = function(e) class(e)[[1L]]
  )
}

fake_r5r_core <- structure(list(), class = c("r5r_core", "list"))

tibble::tibble(
  provider = c("mapbox", "r5r"),
  condition = c(
    condition_class(cacs_isochrone(
      sites = demo_site,
      provider = "mapbox",
      drive_times = 5L,
      mapbox_token = "FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_DOCS",
      verbose = FALSE
    )),
    condition_class(cacs_isochrone(
      sites = demo_site,
      provider = "r5r",
      drive_times = 5L,
      r5r_core = fake_r5r_core,
      verbose = FALSE
    ))
  )
)
# A tibble: 2 × 2
  provider condition
  <chr>    <chr>
1 mapbox   catchmentACS_error_credential
2 r5r      catchmentACS_error_credential

The same release-status principle applies to weight_method = "population": the argument is reserved, but the implementation is not active in this release. It fails loud at the orchestrator boundary, before any network or spatial work begins.

condition_class(cacs_run(
  sites = demo_site,
  state = "AL",
  drive_times = 5L,
  provider = "osrm",
  weight_method = "population",
  verbose = FALSE
))
[1] "catchmentACS_error_credential"

Cache behavior

The persistent cache is useful for live work, especially provider and ACS calls. Vignettes disable it for deterministic no-network rendering.

cacs_get_cache_state() |>
  select(enabled, cache_dir, namespace_mode, counters) |>
  mutate(cache_dir = "<user-cache-dir>/catchmentACS")
# A tibble: 1 × 4
  enabled cache_dir                     namespace_mode counters
  <lgl>   <chr>                         <chr>          <list>
1 FALSE   <user-cache-dir>/catchmentACS production     <tibble [3 × 4]>

For interactive live analysis, the default cache can save repeated requests. A warm ACS cache entry returns without calling Census and without requiring CENSUS_API_KEY; force_refresh = TRUE deliberately bypasses that cache and therefore requires a key. If a live ACS or isochrone input changes and you want a fresh pull, clear the relevant namespace or pass provider/fetch arguments that change the cache key.

cacs_cache_status()
cacs_clear_cache("isochrone", confirm = FALSE)
cacs_clear_cache("acs", confirm = FALSE)

Live full-run template

The full live path is concise. It is non-evaluated here because it calls both a routing provider and Census.

tidycensus::census_api_key("YOUR_KEY_HERE", install = TRUE)

result <- cacs_run(
  sites = cacs_alabama_sites,
  state = "AL",
  year = 2023,
  drive_times = c(5, 10, 15),
  variables = unname(cacs_acs_default_vars),
  provider = "osrm",
  weight_method = "area",
  output = "long",
  verbose = TRUE
)

summary(result)$rates_per_site_moe
attr(result, "cacs_run_provenance")
